results.title: Measuring Faithfulness. Various tests and metrics for quantifying faithfulness of free-text explanations in LMs have previously been proposed (Lanham et al., 2023; Bentham et al., 2024; Atanasova et al., 2023; Siegel et al., 2024). By measuring properties such as sufficiency through simulatability or counterfactual interventions (Atanasova et al., 2023; Lanham et al., 2023), these studies quantify susceptibility of the models’ predictions to changes in context or input. Such approaches are valid only if there is no direct causal link between the input and prediction that bypasses the explanation, which is rare in LMs (Bao et al., 2025). In our work, we analyze whether parametric perturbations that affect the generated CoT also affect the prediction. The closest to ours are the contemporaneous works of Yeo et al. (2024) who use activation patching to measure causal effect of corrupting certain hidden states, and Zaman and Srivastava (2025) who use knowledge editing to evaluate existing (un)faithfulness metrics.

item.text: {"text":"Activation-patching research offers useful methods, but transfer to BERT4Rec remains a hypothesis. [Zhang & Nanda, ICLR 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042) show that corruption choices and measurement metrics can substantially change localization results; [Heimersheim & Nanda, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255) explain complementary clean-to-corrupted and corrupted-to-clean interventions. [MIB, ICML 2025](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/mueller25a.html) evaluates circuit faithfulness across sizes and against random controls. Proposed application: patch attention outputs, feed-forward outputs, and residual states between matched histories; measure target-versus-negative score margins alongside ranking changes. Include identical-input patches, random donor patches, equally sized random component sets, and restoration checks. Layer ablation alone establishes sensitivity to intervention, not a uniquely identified mechanism.\n\nSequential-recommendation evidence motivates separating position and popularity effects: [Learning Positional Attention, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02793) finds learned positional embeddings often encode token distance; [Lin et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.12008) connect popularity amplification to dominant score-matrix spectral components. For the single trained BERT4Rec, proposed controls are item replacement matched on training frequency, history permutation preserving the item multiset, and position-embedding interventions preserving content. Keep left padding and appended-mask readout fixed; patch aligned nonpadding positions. Embedding-norm/frequency correlations are descriptive evidence, requiring controlled interventions before claiming shortcuts. Check activation norms and unchanged unpatched paths to detect intervention artifacts. Report training-prefix mechanism measurements separately from held-out macro validation HR@10: faithful recovery of model behavior does not establish recommendation usefulness."}
